newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-PARCELLS QUITS, PATS OWNER DEMANDS TOP PICK IF JETS WANT HIM.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-PARCELLS QUITS, PATS OWNER DEMANDS TOP PICK IF JETS WANT HIM.

text.p: New England Patriots coach Bill Parcells announced Friday that he would no longer coach the American Football Conference champions and was prepared to sit out the season.
"I have chosen not to extend my contract with the New England Patriots," said Parcells, who led New England to the Super Bowl this year where they lost 35-21 to the Green Bay Packers.

According to the terms of his pact, Parcells will not be allowed to take any other coaching job in 1997 without permission from the Patriots, whose owner warned the New York Jets that any compensation offer for Parcells' services must include the first pick in the NFL draft.
The Jets began preliminary discussions with the Patriots Thursday on possible compensation for Parcells' services.
Patriots team owner Bob Kraft followed Parcells to the podium at Foxboro Stadium for his own news conference.

After thanking Parcells for leading the team from mediocrity to the Super Bowl in four years, he turned his sights on the Jets, who have made it clear they are hoping to put Parcells in charge of their 1-15 team.
Kraft said that for him to consider granting Parcells permission to return to coaching next season "the number one pick must be part of the solution."
As the NFL's worst team last season, the Jets have the first pick in the upcoming draft of college players.

Parcells' announcement comes two days after NFL Commissioner Paul Tagliabue ruled against him in the dispute between the coach and Kraft. Tagliabue ruled that Parcells was contractually bound to the Patriots for the 1997 season and cannot coach another NFL team in 1997 without Kraft's consent.
According to the ruling handed down by Tagliabue, Parcells was ordered to declare by the end of the day Friday whether he wanted to coach the Patriots in 1997.

"I'm grateful for the opportunity to have been here," said Parcells, who had renegotiated his contract before the start of the past season to give him the option of not returning for the fifth and final year of his initial agreement.
"I'm not allowed to coach this year unless it's with the Patriots, the commissioner rendered that decision," said Parcells. "I don't know what I'm going to do."

According to the ruling, Parcells could pursue other business opportunities, such as broadcasting or non-coaching positions. He cannot take a team's general manager's job, then assume the coaching duties one year later.
Parcells would not discuss the possibility of coaching the Jets.
"Why should I deliberate on an option I don't have?" said Parcells. "That's a hypothetical situation. Right now, I'm sitting out."
Before addressing the Jets' situation, Kraft formally thanked Parcells.
"We owe a tremendous debt of gratitude ... for the contributions Bill Parcells has made to this franchise the last four years," said Kraft.
"If Bill Parcells were not the leader of this organisation, I don't think we'd have a chance to be in that (Super Bowl) game."
Parcells has been at odds with Patriots' management over his limited role in selecting players for the team.
Parcells said Kraft had a right to run his team any way he wanted but let show his frustration at not having had the final word on drafting players.
"It's just like a friend of my told me, 'If they want you to make dinner, they should at least let you shop for some of the groceries,'" he said.
